Commentary.Commentary: That brings us to the end of this game. The Kiwis have got their hands on the tri-series with a game to go. The last one is a dead rubber between New Zealand and Bangladesh on 24th May, 2017 at Dublin. Do join us for that match. Until next time, it's goodbye from us. Cheers!

New Zealand skipper and Man of the Match, Tom Latham is really elated with the performance that they have put up today. Is happy to learn from the mistakes that they had committed in the previous matches. Adds they racked up a huge score on the board courtesy a good partnerships which kept on stringing. Feels it's always good to contribute in a winning cause. On the Champions Trophy, he says the preparations have been good and hopes for the best. Ends by saying they have a game left and wants to play good cricket.

Ireland skipper, William Porterfield is disappointed with how things turned out today. Feels they bowled well in patches but couldn't stop the onslaught. Credits Simi Sing for putting up a good show with the ball. Ends by saying that they have been playing good cricket recently and hopes they can continue the same whenever they get an opportunity next time.

So, quite a comprehensive win for New Zealand which has seen them taking an unassailable lead in the tri-series. To be frank, Ireland were never really in the chase. New Zealand kept chipping away at the wickets which made the task all the more difficult for the batsmen. The only positive for the hosts was the 51-run stand between Joyce and Porterfield with the latter scoring 48, highest of the innings. Earlier in the day, Tom Latham led the way for the Kiwis, scoring a ton while Colin Munro's handy cameo down the order helped them cross the 340-run mark. The bowlers then did their job with utmost ease as all of them chipped in with a wicket at least. Matt Henry was the best as he scalped a 3-fer. Stay tuned for the presentation...

Welcome back for the run chase. It was raining just towards the close of the first innings but for now it has stayed away. Let's hope for it remains the same throughout. The Irish openers - Paul Stirling and Ed Joyce are set to open the batting. New Zealand start off with Adam Milne first up. Here we go!!!
